content.value_statement: Developers need clear SDK patterns for persistent Azure AI agents in .NET. This skill provides concise examples for agents, threads, runs, streaming, and tools.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation and environment variable setup for Azure.AI.Agents.Persistent.
Explains PersistentAgentsClient authentication with Azure Identity.
Outlines agent creation, thread messages, polling runs, and streaming updates.
Demonstrates function calling, file search, Bing grounding, and Azure AI Search patterns.
Lists key SDK types, cleanup steps, and RequestFailedException handling.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not a complete runnable project.
It assumes an existing Azure AI project, model deployment, and service connections.
It does not implement the custom function bodies used in examples.
SDK versions and preview APIs may change after the skill was authored.

use_cases.title: Create a First Persistent Agent
use_cases.description: Use the workflow examples to set up a client, create an agent, add a message, and run it.

use_cases.title: Add Agent Tooling
use_cases.description: Compare tool definitions for function calling, file search, Bing grounding, and Azure AI Search integration.

use_cases.title: Review SDK Concepts
use_cases.description: Use the type reference and lifecycle notes to evaluate how persistent agents fit into a .NET service.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a basic Azure AI persistent agent in .NET. Include packages, environment variables, authentication, and the first run steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Streaming Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to adapt my Azure AI Agents .NET workflow from polling to streaming. Explain the update types I should handle.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tool Integrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a .NET persistent agent that uses function calling and file search. Include resource setup, run handling, and cleanup considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure AI Agents .NET architecture for production readiness. Focus on run states, cleanup, error handling, identity, and tool boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need a first persistent agent in a .NET app.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step implementation plan covering packages, Azure Identity, client creation, agent setup, thread creation, message submission, and run polling.

output_examples.input: I want real-time responses from an Azure AI agent.
output_examples.output: A streaming workflow summary that identifies run creation, message content updates, completion handling, and status checks.

output_examples.input: I need to add document search to my agent.
output_examples.output: A design outline for uploading files, creating a vector store, attaching file search resources, and cleaning up agent resources.

best_practices: Use Azure Identity and environment variables for configuration values.
Handle all run states, including required actions, failures, and cancellations.
Delete temporary agents, threads, vector stores, and files when work is complete.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode project endpoints, connection IDs, or deployment names in source files.
Do not ignore required tool actions during long-running agent runs.
Do not leave uploaded files or vector stores unmanaged after tests.

faq.question: What SDK does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.AI.Agents.Persistent for .NET and related Azure AI agent concepts.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources for me?
faq.answer: No. It shows SDK usage patterns and assumes your Azure project and connections already exist.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The generated marketplace metadata marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include streaming guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a streaming response section and lists common streaming update types.

faq.question: Does it explain agent tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers function calling, file search, Bing grounding, Azure AI Search, and other available tools.

faq.question: Is this a security hardening guide?
faq.answer: No. It includes some operational best practices, but it is mainly an SDK reference.
